headline: Machine learning models infer gene regulation from single-cell and sequence data
label: Single Cell Gene Regulatory Inference
summary: Single-cell multiomics and sequence-based deep models now jointly resolve enhancer-driven regulatory programs across cell types.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational inference of regulatory architecture from single-cell and sequence data. SPARK applies Bayesian DAG structure learning to single-cell multiome data to reconstruct enhancer-based networks using prior knowledge, while scHGNN infers gene regulatory networks from scRNA-seq by fusing expression with multi-order network topology. Scooby-2 fine-tunes AlphaGenome with a cell-specific decoder to predict single-cell RNA-seq and chromatin accessibility tracks from DNA sequence, and XChrom predicts single-cell accessibility across unseen regions and cells. Regularized and interpretable models recur elsewhere: DisTwiner applies subgroup-aware Elastic Net to macrophage scRNA-seq, and xNNPCD links perturbation transcriptomes to dependency profiles. A PANDA/LIONESS benchmark of clustering strategies addresses patient-specific networks across 9,778 tumors from 33 cancer types.
